scope: Theorem 6.1 (Promised norm solver) of the manuscript “Deterministic Polynomial Factorization over Prime Fields” (preprints/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields-October-4-2026/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 142 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ed88aa5ba802311a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let k be an explicitly represented finite field of characteristic p, let q be an odd prime, and suppose that a primitive qth root of unity ζ ∈ k and a generator of the full q-primary subgroup of k∗ are given. Let F ∈ k[X] be monic and square-free, of positive degree N divisible by q. Put K0 = k(X), L = K0[Y ]/(Y q − F), ρ(Y ) = ζY. Let G ∈ K∗ 0 , write D for the maximum of its reduced numerator and denominator degrees, and assume p > (N + 2D + 1)2 . (6.1) If G belongs to NormL/K0 (L∗), a deterministic algorithm constructs h ∈ L∗ with q−1 Y j=0 ρj (h) = G. Its bit complexity, and the degrees of the rational coefficients of h in the basis 1, Y, . . . , Y q−1, are bounded by fixed polynomials in q, N, D, and log |k|. It uses no polynomial factoriza- tion oracle. Its field-dependent branches use only zero tests, so the algorithm admits the simultaneous execution of Lemma 2.1.
